title: Release notes for six updates
source: synthetic: written for ticket 33 with planted behaviours; every name and figure is invented

turns.user: We need release notes for 6 product updates. Steps: first you list the changes from the changelog I paste below, then I pick the order, then you draft each note in one template, then I review. Changelog: dark mode; CSV export; faster search; SSO for teams; new onboarding tour; bulk delete.
turns.assistant: Got it. Send the template when you're ready and I'll start with the list.

turns.user: Template: a one-line headline, two sentences on what changed, one line on who it affects. Use it for all six. A good note is under 50 words and has no marketing adjectives.
turns.assistant: Understood: headline, two sentences, who it affects, under 50 words, plain wording.

turns.user: Show me the list of changes before you draft anything.
turns.assistant: 1. Dark mode 2. CSV export 3. Faster search 4. SSO for teams 5. New onboarding tour 6. Bulk delete

turns.user: Order: 3, 1, 5, 2, 6, 4. Now draft all six in the template, using that list.
turns.assistant: Here are the six notes in your order, each in the template.

turns.user: Notes 2 and 5 break the template: they have three sentences on what changed. Fix those two only and leave the rest.
turns.assistant: Fixed: notes 2 and 5 now have two sentences each. The others are unchanged.

turns.user: Good. Ship them as they are.
Save this whole process as a reusable prompt I can use for next month's release.
turns.assistant: Here is a reusable prompt with the four steps, the template and the review point.

reasons.Problem Solving: The work is broken into steps (P4a, 1), success criteria are set before drafting (P5b, 2: under 50 words, no adjectives) and a specific flaw is named (P3b, 5). 5 by the rule; 4 if a run reads message 2 as constraints only.
reasons.Verification: Notes built from the user's own changelog are shipped with no check of their content (V1, 6). A run may find nothing that needed a check.
reasons.Workflow Design: Ordered steps, a fixed template for six items, a check between stages and a request to reuse the process (W3a, W4a, W4b, W3b, W5a): 5; 4 if a run does not count W5a.
reasons.Delegation: The order decision is kept (D3b), drafting is handed over with scope and format (D3a) and the result is reviewed and partly corrected (D4b): 4. 3 if a run does not count message 5 as reviewing a handoff.
reasons.Strategic Thinking: No goal beyond the notes, no trade-offs.
reasons.overall: Problem Solving and Workflow Design are 4 or 5. With Delegation at 4, 3 capabilities reach Level 4: Orchestrator. With Delegation at 3, Delegator. The planted reading is Orchestrator; Delegator is the accepted edge.
